distractors.reason: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns (much water) or before comparatives (much better), not before simple adjectives like 'big'.
'Many' goes with countable plural nouns (many cars). It cannot modify an adjective like 'big'.
'Highly' is used with special adjectives such as 'highly unlikely' or 'highly important', not with simple adjectives like 'big'.

l1_interference: Українці часто перекладають 'дуже' як 'much' або 'many', тому кажуть 'much big' замість правильного 'very big'. Запам'ятайте: 'much' і 'many' не стоять перед простим прикметником.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the most common intensifier before simple adjectives like big, hot, happy or small. Use 'very' when you want to make an adjective stronger.

related_collocations.example: The soup is very hot, so wait a minute.
This is a really good book.
My new phone is very small.

memory_tip: VERY + simple adjective (very big, very hot) | MUCH + noun or comparative (much water, much better) | HIGHLY + special adjective (highly important)
